name: A Tale in the Desert
summary: A combat-free MMO set in ancient Egypt in which players gather, craft, and build, pass tests in several disciplines, and govern the world through player-written petitions and votes, with the world wiped and restarted at the end of each Telling.

name: Against the Storm
summary: A roguelite city builder in which each settlement must fill a reputation gauge before the Queen's impatience runs out, balancing three villager species' needs while opening dangerous forest glades under a recurring blightstorm.

name: AI Dungeon
summary: A text adventure in which a large language model continues the story after each player input, so actions, dialogue, and world facts the player types are improvised into narration rather than resolved by authored rules.

name: Animal Crossing: New Horizons
summary: A Nintendo life sim on a deserted island whose clock, seasons, and wildlife follow the real calendar, built around gathering, D.I.Y. crafting, museum collections, villager relationships, and island design.

name: Anno 117: Pax Romana
summary: A Roman-era Anno city builder in which residents advance from Liberti to Patricians through categorized needs, buildings affect their neighbors, schools generate research, and modular ships guard multi-island trade.

name: Anno 1800
summary: An industrial-era city builder in which residents advance through five Old World tiers by consuming goods from multi-island production chains, linked to a New World session by trade routes and contested by AI rivals.

name: Arma 3
summary: A first-person military simulation on large open terrains in which infantry, vehicles, and aircraft fight under modeled ballistics, recoil, and load-based stamina, extended by the Eden editor, SQF scripting, and a large mod community.

name: Aurora 4X
summary: A free space 4X simulation by a single developer in which the player runs an interstellar empire through ship design from components, mineral mining, sensor-based detection, missile and beam combat, and named officers, with time advanced in steps from seconds to days.

name: Autonauts
summary: A colony automation game in which the player crafts workerbots from parts and teaches them farming, crafting, and cooking routines in a Scratch-style visual language, so that bots supply the food, housing, and care that a growing population of Folk needs.

name: Balance of Power
summary: A Cold War geopolitical sim in which the player, as US or Soviet leader, spends aid, treaties, and interventions on minor countries over eight annual turns and manages escalating crises to gain prestige without triggering nuclear war.

name: Banished
summary: A survival city builder without money or a tech tree in which exiled families gather, farm, and stockpile for winter while aging, births, disease, and disasters decide whether the town grows or starves.

name: BeamNG.drive
summary: A vehicle sim built on soft-body physics in which every vehicle is a node-and-beam skeleton that flexes, deforms, and breaks under impact, played as a free-roam sandbox with scenarios.

name: Besiege
summary: A physics construction game where the player builds medieval siege machines from blocks, wheels, and weapons, then drives them against castles and armies in objective levels or a sandbox.

name: Big Ambitions
summary: A business life sim set in a simulated New York City in which the player's avatar rents storefronts, stocks and staffs shops, builds warehouse logistics, and grows from one store into a business empire.

name: Big Pharma
summary: A pharmaceutical factory and business sim in which the player routes ingredients through machines on conveyor belts to push their concentration into the range that activates cures while suppressing side effects, then sells into contested markets.

name: Bitburner
summary: A free, open-source incremental hacking game in which the player writes JavaScript scripts that hack, grow, and weaken simulated servers for money, then spends it with faction reputation on augmentations that reset progress in exchange for permanent multipliers.

name: Black & White
summary: A god game in which the player wins villagers' belief through miracles, help, or fear while training a giant creature whose behavior is learned from the player's rewards and punishments.

name: Caesar III
summary: A Roman city builder in which service walkers roam the roads from their buildings, houses evolve only where food, goods, and services actually reach them, and missions are won on culture, prosperity, peace, and favor ratings.

name: Capitalism
summary: A corporate business sim in which the player builds retail stores, factories, farms, mines, and R&D centers from internal unit layouts and competes with AI firms on price, quality, and brand across city markets.

name: Captain of Industry
summary: An industrial colony builder in which the player reshapes island terrain with excavators and trucks, runs production chains to feed, house, and power a settlement, and spends the Unity its satisfied population generates on edicts, quick builds, and world-map expansion.

name: Car Mechanic Simulator 2021
summary: A first-person garage sim in which the player diagnoses and repairs customer cars part by part, restores auction and barn-find cars, and expands the workshop.

name: Caves of Qud
summary: A science-fantasy roguelike RPG with simulated factions, liquids, body parts, and procedurally generated histories, built partly with wave function collapse.

name: Cities: Skylines
summary: A city builder in which road-following zones, agent citizens who route to work along computed paths, district policies, and player-drawn transit lines make traffic flow the central design problem.

name: Cities: Skylines II
summary: The sequel to Cities: Skylines, with citizens choosing routes by time, comfort, and money, a tech tree of development points, preset climates with seasons, and maps of up to 441 tiles.

name: Sid Meier's Civilization
summary: A turn-based 4X game in which the player guides a civilization from 4000 BC toward the space age by founding cities, researching a technology tree, building one-per-world wonders, and competing with rival civilizations by diplomacy or war.

name: Command: Modern Operations
summary: A real-time operational military simulation in which the player commands air, naval, and land units drawn from a database of tens of thousands of real platforms, sensors, and weapons on a map of Earth, managing doctrine, emissions control, and missions.

name: Contraband Police
summary: A first-person border-post sim set in 1981 in which the player checks drivers' documents, searches vehicles for hidden contraband, chases smugglers, and upgrades the post against gang attacks.

name: Creatures
summary: An artificial-life game in which the player hatches and raises Norns whose neural-network brains, simulated biochemistry, and haploid digital genomes produce learned behavior and heritable mutation.

name: Crusader Kings III
summary: A character-driven grand strategy game in which the player rules as successive heads of a medieval dynasty from 867 or later to 1453, managing traits, stress, vassal opinion, marriages, and succession across a map of feudal titles.

name: DCS World
summary: A combat flight sim platform of study-level aircraft modules with clickable cockpits and modeled subsystems, flown in missions and on multiplayer servers built with a Lua-scriptable mission editor.

name: Democracy 4
summary: A turn-based government sim in which the player, as leader of a democracy, adjusts policy sliders whose weighted effects move statistics and overlapping voter groups, resolves dilemmas, and tries to balance the budget and win the next election.

name: Don't Starve
summary: A survival sim in a procedurally generated wilderness where the player balances hunger, health, and sanity, crafts tools and light, and prepares for darkness, hounds, and seasons.

name: Dwarf Fortress
summary: A colony sim in which the player directs a fortress of autonomous dwarves inside a procedurally generated world whose history, geology, fluids, bodies, and minds are all simulated.

name: Dyson Sphere Program
summary: A 3D factory automation game in which the player's mech builds production lines on rotating planets, links star systems with logistics drones and warp vessels, and launches sails and rockets to assemble Dyson spheres around stars.

name: Eco
summary: A multiplayer civilization survival game in which players on one server share a simulated ecosystem, specialize in skills, craft and trade with player-made currencies, and pass enforceable laws while researching how to stop a meteor due in thirty days without wrecking the environment.

name: Elite
summary: A 3D space trading and combat game in which the player flies a single ship through eight seed-generated galaxies, buying and selling cargo and fighting pirates and police to raise a combat rating.

name: Elite Dangerous
summary: An online space sim set in a 1:1 procedurally generated Milky Way where players trade, fight, mine, and explore while a server-side background simulation shifts faction control from aggregate player actions.

name: Equilinox
summary: A relaxed nature-building game in which the player spreads biomes with grasses, places plants and animals that each have environmental requirements, and spends diversity points earned by healthy species on evolutions and genetic modifications.

name: Euro Truck Simulator 2
summary: A truck driving sim in which the player hauls timed cargo deliveries across a scaled European road network and grows a transport company of trucks, garages, and hired drivers.

name: Europa Universalis IV
summary: A real-time-with-pause grand strategy game in which the player directs one of over 500 nations from 1444 to 1821 through monarch-point spending, trade-node competition, colonization, diplomacy, and war on a province map.

name: EVE Online
summary: A single-universe space MMO in which players mine, manufacture, trade, and fight in ships that are destroyed for good, inside a player-made economy and a galaxy of high-, low-, and null-security space where player alliances claim sovereignty.

name: Façade
summary: A free 2005 interactive drama in which the player types natural language as a dinner guest of the married couple Grace and Trip while a drama manager sequences authored beats toward one of three endings.

name: Factorio
summary: A factory automation game in which the player builds belt, train, robot, and circuit networks that mine, refine, and assemble items on an alien planet while pollution provokes native biters that evolve over time.

name: Farming Simulator 25
summary: The 2024 entry in Giants Software's series in which the player runs a farm business by operating over 400 licensed vehicles and implements across seasonal field work, livestock, forestry, and production chains.

name: Farthest Frontier
summary: A frontier-town city builder in which crop rotation, soil fertility, diet variety, clean water, and healers decide whether named diseases spread, while prosperity draws stronger raiders against walled defenses.

name: Football Manager
summary: A football club management series in which the player sets tactics, training, transfers, and finances while a match engine simulates games from the attributes of players drawn from a researched database of real footballers.

name: Foundation
summary: A gridless medieval city builder in which painted zones grow homes organically, monuments are assembled from modular parts, and the village advances along Labor, Clergy, or Kingdom estates.

name: From Dust
summary: A god game in which the player carries sand, water, and lava across islands whose material simulation erodes, floods, and hardens terrain, protecting a tribe as it founds villages at totems.

name: Frostpunk
summary: A survival city builder in which the leader of the last city around a coal generator must keep falling temperatures at bay while signing laws that trade citizens' welfare against productivity under hope and discontent meters.

name: Frostpunk 2
summary: The sequel to Frostpunk, in which the Steward builds whole districts on the frost and must pass laws through a council of 100 faction delegates while faction tension can escalate into civil war.

name: FTL: Faster Than Light
summary: A roguelite starship sim where the player allocates reactor power and directs crew through room-level oxygen, fire, breach, and system-damage simulation while fleeing a rebel fleet across eight sectors.

name: Game Dev Tycoon
summary: A game-studio business sim where the player picks topic, genre, and platform for each game, splits development effort across design and technology focus areas, and lives or dies by review scores across the history of the industry.

name: Conway's Game of Life
summary: A zero-player cellular automaton on an infinite square grid in which each cell lives or dies by the B3/S23 neighbor-count rule, producing gliders, oscillators, and universal computation from a seeded pattern.

name: Garry's Mod
summary: A Source engine physics sandbox in which players spawn props, ragdolls, and NPCs, join them with welds and constraints, and script whole new multiplayer game modes in Lua.

name: Generative Agents (Smallville)
summary: A research sandbox in which 25 language-model agents in a Sims-like town keep natural-language memory streams, reflect, and plan their days, producing unscripted information spread and social coordination.

name: Going Medieval
summary: A colony sim set after a plague in which settlers with traits, needs, and moods dig into and build up a multi-level voxel terrain to survive seasons and raids.

name: Gran Turismo
summary: A PlayStation racing game that paired a tuned handling model and 140 production cars with license tests, prize credits, and parts tuning in a Simulation mode career.

name: Gran Turismo 7
summary: A console racing simulator that combines a detailed vehicle dynamics model and car collection with GT Sophy, a deep reinforcement learning opponent added as a permanent rival in 2023.

name: Hamurabi
summary: A ten-turn text game in which the player, as the Babylonian king Hammurabi, splits a grain stock between feeding people, planting acres, and buying land while harvests, rats, and plague vary at random.

name: Hardspace: Shipbreaker
summary: A zero-gravity salvage sim in which the player cuts derelict ships apart with a laser cutter and grapple, manages decompression and volatile systems, and sorts salvage to pay down a large debt.

name: Harvest Moon
summary: An early farming sim for the Super Famicom in which the player has two and a half years to restore an inherited farm through daily crop watering, livestock care, and courting one of five eligible women.

name: Hearts of Iron IV
summary: A World War II grand strategy game starting in 1936 or 1939 in which the player builds factories, turns resources into equipment, designs divisions, follows a national focus tree, and directs fronts and battle plans across land, sea, and air.

name: House Flipper
summary: A first-person renovation sim in which the player cleans, paints, demolishes, and furnishes rundown houses, then sells them to buyers whose bids depend on how well the house fits their needs.

name: Infinite Craft
summary: A browser crafting game in which combining any two elements yields a new element whose name and emoji a language model generates on first request and a shared database then fixes for all players.

name: inZOI
summary: A Krafton life sim in early access since March 2025 in which the player oversees autonomous Zois with eight needs in dense cities, with optional on-device language model prompts and generative tools for patterns and objects.

name: iRacing
summary: A subscription online racing sim with laser-scanned cars and tracks in which drivers race scheduled official series and advance through license classes gated by a no-fault Safety Rating, while an Elo-style iRating sorts fields.

name: Islanders
summary: A minimalist placement puzzle in which every building scores points from compatible and incompatible neighbors on a procedural island, and score thresholds unlock new building packs and new islands.

name: Job Simulator
summary: A room-scale VR comedy set in a museum run by robots, where the player performs parodied office, kitchen, store, and garage tasks by grabbing and manipulating physics objects.

name: Jurassic World Evolution
summary: A dinosaur park management game in which the player excavates fossils for DNA, breeds and modifies dinosaurs, and keeps them contained through storms, sabotage, and breakouts while balancing three division contracts.

name: Kenshi
summary: A squad-based open-world RPG with no hero character, where any recruit can starve, lose limbs, train skills by doing, be enslaved, or found an outpost among reactive factions.

name: Kerbal Space Program
summary: A space flight sim where the player assembles rockets from parts and flies them under patched-conic orbital physics and atmospheric aerodynamics through a scaled-down planetary system.

name: Kingdoms and Castles
summary: A medieval town builder in which peasants farm and stockpile for an annual winter while the player stacks castle blocks into walls and towers to defend against vikings, dragons, and ogres.

name: Lemonade Stand
summary: A 1973 educational business sim in which the player runs a lemonade stand for 12 days, setting glasses made, advertising signs, and price against a daily weather report.

name: Little Computer People
summary: A 1985 home-computer life sim in which one procedurally seeded little person lives in a cross-section of a three-story house, follows a daily routine, and depends on the player for food, water, and attention.

name: Manor Lords
summary: An early-access medieval city builder in which families settle gridless burgage plots along curved roads, fields depend on soil fertility and crop rotation, and the lord fields retinue and militia in real-time battles.

name: Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020)
summary: A flight sim that streams a photorealistic model of the whole Earth built from map and photogrammetry data and flies aircraft through live weather with a surface-level aerodynamic model.

name: Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024
summary: The successor to Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020) that adds a career mode of certified aviation jobs, walk-around preflight, revised aircraft systems, and modeled ground surfaces to the streamed whole-Earth flight sim.

name: Mindustry
summary: An open-source automation tower defense game in which the player belts ore into factories that supply turrets, units, and the core against enemy waves while capturing campaign sectors on two planets, with an assembly-like logic language for controlling blocks and units.

name: Minecraft
summary: A procedurally generated voxel sandbox where players mine blocks, craft tools, survive hostile night mobs and hunger, farm and trade, and build circuits from redstone.

name: Mini Metro
summary: A minimalist subway-design game where the player draws and redraws lines between shape-coded stations under a weekly ration of trains and tunnels until a station overcrowds.

name: Motorsport Manager
summary: A racing team management game in which the player designs car parts across seasons, hires drivers and staff, and makes live strategy calls on tyres, pit stops, and weather while races are simulated.

name: M.U.L.E.
summary: A four-player economic strategy game on a colony planet where players outfit M.U.L.E. robots to produce food, energy, smithore, and crystite and trade them in real-time auctions.

name: Nintendogs
summary: A Nintendo DS puppy sim in which the player pets, washes, feeds, and walks up to three dogs, teaches them tricks with recorded voice commands, and enters disc, agility, and obedience trials.

name: Noita
summary: A roguelite action game in which every pixel of the world is simulated as a falling-sand material that burns, melts, flows, and reacts, and the player builds wands from spells to dig through procedurally generated levels.

name: Offworld Trading Company
summary: A real-time economic strategy game on Mars where companies claim resource tiles, refine goods for a shared market whose prices move with every trade, and win by buying out every rival's stock.

name: Opus Magnum
summary: A programming puzzle game in which the player builds alchemical machines from arms, tracks, and glyphs on a hex grid, programs them on an instruction timeline, and compares each looping solution's cost, cycles, and area against other players' histograms.

name: The Oregon Trail
summary: An educational turn-based travel sim in which the player buys supplies and sets rations for a wagon journey to Oregon while random events, weather, and illness threaten the party.

name: Out of the Park Baseball
summary: A text-based baseball management sim in which the player runs a franchise's roster, scouting, draft, trades, and finances while a pitch-by-pitch engine simulates games for career, historical, or fictional leagues.

name: Oxygen Not Included
summary: A side-view colony sim in which a few duplicants survive inside an asteroid where every tile holds an element with mass and temperature, so air, liquids, heat, and germs flow through the base.

name: Papers, Please
summary: A border inspection game in which the player checks entrants' documents against daily-changing rules on a timed shift and spends the wages on a family's rent, food, and heat.

name: Paralives
summary: An indie life sim, in early access since May 2026, in which players build grid-less homes and guide Parafolks with needs, emotions, traits, skills, and careers in an open-world town.

name: PC Building Simulator
summary: A workshop sim in which the player takes email jobs to build, upgrade, repair, and overclock PCs from licensed parts and verifies the results with benchmark software.

name: Pharaoh
summary: An Egyptian city builder on the Caesar III engine in which a yearly Nile flood waters floodplain farms, walkers carry services to housing, five gods must be appeased, and monuments take years of labor and materials.

name: Plague Inc.
summary: A strategy game in which the player evolves a pathogen's transmission, symptoms, and abilities to infect and kill the world's population before humanity's cure research finishes.

name: Planet Coaster
summary: A 3D theme park builder with a spline and piece coaster editor, modular scenery, and individually simulated guests and staff, built around sharing creations through the Steam Workshop.

name: Planet Zoo
summary: A zoo management game where the player builds habitats to meet each species' welfare needs, manages genetics and breeding, and raises a conservation rating, using Planet Coaster's building tools.

name: Poly Bridge
summary: A bridge-building puzzle game where the player places beams and roads from materials with different costs and strengths under a budget, then runs a physics test as vehicles cross.

name: Populous
summary: The first god game, in which the player raises and lowers land so followers can build and multiply, then spends the mana they generate on disasters against a rival deity's people.

name: PowerWash Simulator
summary: A first-person cleaning sim in which the player power-washes vehicles and buildings, choosing nozzles and soaps to strip dirt layers until every part reports clean.

name: Princess Maker 2
summary: A raising sim in which the player, as a father figure, schedules a daughter's training, part-time jobs, rest, and adventures from age 10 to 18, and her accumulated attributes decide one of 74 endings.

name: Prison Architect
summary: A prison management sim in which the player builds a facility, sets an hourly regime, and staffs it while hundreds of prisoners pursue needs whose neglect leads to fights, escapes, and riots.

name: Project Hospital
summary: A hospital management sim in which the player builds departments and hires staff while doctors diagnose patients by ordering examinations that reveal symptoms until one diagnosis remains.

name: Project Sid
summary: An Altera research demonstration that runs 10 to 1,000-plus language-model agents with the concurrent PIANO architecture in Minecraft to study role specialization, collective rule-making, and cultural transmission.

name: Project Zomboid
summary: An isometric zombie survival sandbox in which one survivor manages moodles, injuries, skills, and failing utilities across a large Kentucky map until an inevitable death.

name: Prom Week
summary: A 2012 browser social sim in which the player picks social exchanges among 18 high school students in the week before prom, with the Comme il Faut rule system deciding who wants to do what and how targets respond.

name: Railroad Tycoon
summary: A railroad business sim in which the player lays track, builds stations, schedules trains to meet regional supply and demand, and battles rival barons through the stock market.

name: Rebel Inc.
summary: A counterinsurgency strategy game in which the player, as a coalition governor, spends a monthly budget on civilian and military initiatives to build popular support and stabilize regions of a war-torn country while corruption, inflation, and an insurgency push back.

name: Reigns
summary: A swipe-based card game in which the player, as a succession of medieval monarchs, accepts or rejects advisers' requests that push church, people, army, and treasury meters, and each reign ends when any meter empties or fills.

name: RimWorld
summary: A colony sim where a few named colonists with needs, traits, injuries, and relationships survive on a frontier planet while a storyteller AI paces events.

name: RollerCoaster Tycoon
summary: An amusement park management game in which the player builds rides and custom coasters piece by piece, rated for excitement, intensity, and nausea, to satisfy guests with individual preferences and meet scenario goals.

name: Satisfactory
summary: A first-person 3D factory automation game in which a pioneer taps infinite resource nodes on an alien planet and connects machines with belts, pipes, trains, and drones to deliver project parts to FICSIT's Space Elevator.

name: Schedule I
summary: A first-person crime business sim in which the player grows and cooks drugs, mixes ingredients to create products with effects customers want, sells them around a city under police pressure, and automates production with hired staff.

name: Screeps
summary: A persistent MMO strategy game in which players control colonies only by writing JavaScript that the server runs every tick, directing creeps assembled from body parts to harvest energy, upgrade room controllers, trade, and fight other players' code under a CPU budget.

name: Seaman
summary: A Dreamcast virtual pet in which the player talks through a microphone to a sardonic human-faced fish, managing its tank's heat, water, and food while it matures through five life stages.

name: Second Life
summary: A persistent 3D virtual world in which residents build objects from prims and meshes, script them in the Linden Scripting Language, own land in server-simulated regions, and trade goods and land for Linden Dollars exchangeable for real currency.

name: shapez 2
summary: A combat-free factory automation game in which the player builds multi-level factories on space platforms that cut, rotate, stack, and paint layered geometric shapes and deliver them to a central Vortex to meet escalating milestone and operator goals.

name: Silent Hunter III
summary: A World War II U-boat sim with a dynamic campaign that generates convoys and escorts, manual torpedo targeting, and a persistent crew that gains rank, experience, and morale across patrols.

name: SimAnt
summary: A Maxis ant-colony simulation in which the player controls one yellow ant that lays trails and recruits nestmates while managing a black colony's castes against a rival red colony, predators, and the household.

name: SimCity
summary: The city builder in which a mayor zones residential, commercial, and industrial land, lays power and roads, and sets taxes while grid maps of land value, crime, pollution, and traffic drive where the city grows.

name: SimCity 2000
summary: The isometric sequel to SimCity that adds terrain elevation, an underground layer of water pipes and subways, separate zone tax rates, bonds, ordinances, and power plants that age out.

name: SimCity (2013)
summary: A SimCity reboot built on the agent-based GlassBox engine, in which agents carry workers, power, water, and goods between buildings and small cities share a region over an always-online connection.

name: SimCity 4
summary: A city builder in which several cities share a region map and trade utilities, while zones develop by density and wealth level and a commute model routes trips across roads and transit.

name: SimEarth
summary: A planetary god game built on James Lovelock's Gaia hypothesis in which geology, atmosphere, climate, life, and civilization models interact over billions of years under the player's parameter changes and interventions.

name: SimLife
summary: A Maxis artificial-life toy in which the player edits plant and animal genes, landscape, and the world's physical parameters, then watches food chains and evolution play out.

name: SimTower
summary: A skyscraper management game in which the player stacks offices, condos, hotels, and shops and designs elevator service so tenants on daily routines do not wait long enough to stress out and leave.

name: SnowRunner
summary: An off-road trucking sim in which the player hauls cargo across mud, snow, and water whose surfaces deform under each truck's weight and tires, upgrading a fleet to reach harder terrain.

name: Songs of Syx
summary: A low-fantasy city builder in which tens of thousands of individually simulated citizens and slaves of several races live in a growing city-state whose armies of up to 50,000 units fight real-time battles.

name: Space Engineers
summary: A voxel sandbox where players mine asteroids and planets and build ships and stations block by block, with every block carrying mass, inertia, power needs, and damage under Newtonian physics.

name: Space Haven
summary: A spaceship colony sim in which the player builds a ship tile by tile and keeps a crew with needs, moods, and relationships alive inside a tile-based simulation of oxygen, CO2, heat, and power.

name: SpaceChem
summary: A programming puzzle game in which the player lays out instruction paths for two waldos in grid reactors that grab, bond, rotate, and split atoms into target molecules, with each solution scored on cycles, reactors, and instructions against global histograms.

name: Species: Artificial Life, Real Evolution
summary: A solo-developed evolution simulator in which creatures defined by numeric genes mutate, breed, and speciate in real time across a 3D world while the player observes, edits the gene pool, and alters climate.

name: Spore
summary: A five-stage game in which the player guides a species from cell to galactic empire, building its body, vehicles, and buildings in part-based editors whose creations are shared automatically through the Sporepedia.

name: Stardew Valley
summary: A farming and life sim in which the player restores an inherited farm over four 28-day seasons, splitting a daily energy budget among crops, animals, mining, fishing, and friendships with Pelican Town's residents.

name: Stationeers
summary: A first-person space station survival game whose core is an atmospheric simulation of gas mixtures, pressure, temperature, and combustion that the player must engineer with pipes, power, and programmable logic.

name: Stellaris
summary: A real-time-with-pause space 4X and grand strategy game in which the player designs a species and empire, expands across a procedurally generated hyperlane galaxy from 2200, manages pops, jobs, ethics-based factions, and research card draws, and faces late-game crises.

name: Subnautica
summary: An underwater survival game on an ocean planet where the player manages oxygen, food, and water while crafting tools, submersibles, and bases to explore deeper and escape.

name: Suck Up!
summary: A voice-controlled comedy game in which the player, as a disguised vampire, talks AI-driven townspeople into letting them inside, with each resident's replies generated by a language model from its personality and the player's words.

name: Surgeon Simulator
summary: A physics comedy surgery game in which the player controls one hand with separate finger keys to perform transplants on the patient Bob before his vital signs fail.

name: Surviving Mars
summary: A Mars colony city builder in which drones build power, water, and oxygen networks before colonists with traits arrive in domes, while research, Earth sponsors, and dust storms, meteors, and cold waves shape survival.

name: Suzerain
summary: A text-based political narrative game in which the player, as newly elected President Anton Rayne of Sordland, makes dialogue and policy choices across one term that shift the budget, foreign alignment, and constitutional reform toward one of several endings.

name: Tamagotchi
summary: A 1996 keychain virtual pet whose hunger, happiness, and training meters run on a real-time clock, and whose care quality determines which adult form it grows into and how long it lives.

name: Teardown
summary: A heist and destruction game set in fully destructible voxel levels where the player plans a route by cutting, smashing, and driving through structures, then races a 60-second alarm timer to grab the targets.

name: Terra Nil
summary: A reverse city builder in which the player places machines to clean toxic soil, restore water, and grow biomes on a barren map, then recycles every building and leaves.

name: The Farmer Was Replaced
summary: A programming game in which the player writes Python-like code for a farming drone on a grid farm, where every operation costs simulated ticks, and harvests crops to buy unlocks for language features, farm size, more drones, and new crops.

name: The Incredible Machine
summary: A Rube Goldberg puzzle game in which the player places supplied parts such as balls, ropes, pulleys, belts, and animals into a level so that a deterministic physics run completes a simple goal.

name: The Long Dark
summary: A first-person wilderness survival sim set in frozen northern Canada where the player manages warmth, calories, thirst, fatigue, and afflictions against cold, weather, and wildlife.

name: The Powder Toy
summary: An open-source falling-sand sandbox where hundreds of elements interact cell by cell under simulated air pressure, heat, gravity, and electricity.

name: The Sims
summary: A life sim in which the player builds a house and guides a household of Sims whose decaying motives, personalities, careers, and relationships produce an open-ended domestic story.

name: The Sims 2
summary: The 3D sequel to The Sims that adds aging through seven life stages, genetic inheritance, aspirations with wants and fears, and memories, so households play across generations.

name: The Sims 3
summary: The third mainline Sims game, which places households in a seamless open neighborhood where unplayed Sims keep living, and replaces personality sliders with up to five traits and mood with stacked moodlets.

name: The Sims 4
summary: The fourth mainline Sims game, built around a dominant emotion computed from moodlets, three-trait personalities with aspiration rewards, multitasking, room-based building, and an in-game Gallery for sharing creations.

name: Theme Hospital
summary: A hospital management game where the player builds rooms, hires and trains staff, and routes patients with comic diseases through diagnosis and treatment to meet level goals.

name: Theme Park
summary: A theme park management game in which the player builds rides and shops, tunes prices and recipes for individually simulated visitors, and sells parks to expand worldwide.

name: This War of Mine
summary: A survival sim about civilians in a besieged city who maintain a shelter by day, scavenge by night, and face moral choices that change their mood until a randomized ceasefire.

name: Timberborn
summary: A city builder for beaver colonies in which simulated water flows over terrain, recurring droughts and toxic badtides cut or poison it, and players dam, channel, and store water while building upward.

name: Tiny Glade
summary: A medieval building sandbox in which drawn walls, paths, and building outlines are assembled by procedural rules into detailed castles and cottages, with no goals, management, or failure states.

name: Tomodachi Life
summary: A Nintendo 3DS life sim in which player-made Mii characters live in an island apartment building, form friendships, quarrels, and romances on their own, and ask the player to solve their problems.

name: Townscaper
summary: A town-building toy in which clicking colored blocks onto an irregular grid lets a wave function collapse solver assemble houses, arches, stairways, bridges, and gardens, with no goals or resources.

name: Transport Tycoon
summary: A transport business sim in which the player builds road, rail, sea, and air networks between towns and industries over a century, earning by delivery speed and distance while vehicles age and break down.

name: Tropico 6
summary: A political city builder in which El Presidente develops an island archipelago across four eras while individually simulated citizens' happiness and faction loyalties decide elections, protests, and revolts.

name: Two Point Hospital
summary: A hospital management game and spiritual successor to Theme Hospital in which the player builds rooms, trains staff with traits and qualifications, and cures comic illnesses across a chain of hospitals.

name: Ultima Online
summary: A persistent fantasy MMO in which players progress through skills without classes or levels, craft goods for a player-driven economy, own persistent houses, and could attack each other anywhere until the 2000 split into Trammel and Felucca.

name: Universe Sandbox
summary: A space physics sandbox where the player builds and alters star systems and watches Newtonian n-body gravity, collisions, and simplified planetary climate play out at adjustable speed.

name: Utopia
summary: A two-player Intellivision strategy game in which rival island rulers spend gold on buildings and boats in timed rounds, scoring points for how well their populations are housed, fed, and kept content.

name: Valheim
summary: A co-op Viking survival game in a seeded procedural world of biomes where players gather, build structurally supported shelters, eat for stat buffs, and defeat biome bosses to progress.

name: Versu
summary: A 2013 iPad interactive story platform from Linden Lab in which the player controls one character among autonomous agents who choose actions by simulating their outcomes against hundreds of desires within authored social practices.

name: Victoria 3
summary: An economic grand strategy game set from 1836 to 1936 in which the player industrializes a nation by building production chains, passing laws through interest-group politics, and pursuing diplomatic plays while population strata respond through wages, needs, and radicalism.

name: Viva Piñata
summary: A garden sim in which the player shapes terrain, plants, and water to attract 60 piñata species, then meets each species' requirements to make them residents, breed them, and manage the predators among them.

name: Where Winds Meet
summary: An open-world martial-arts RPG whose NPCs answer free-text and voice chat through a live language model, included as an early large-audience deployment of runtime LLM characters.

name: Whispers from the Star
summary: A voice-driven sci-fi narrative game in which the player helps stranded astronaut Stella survive on the planet Gaia through open-ended spoken or typed conversation answered by an AI-generated, voiced performance.

name: Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic
summary: A planned-economy city builder in which every building, commodity, and citizen moves through explicit logistics, from construction materials delivered by truck to exports at border customs for rubles or dollars.

name: X-Plane
summary: A flight sim whose flight model computes forces on small elements of each wing, control surface, and propeller from aircraft geometry, used for entertainment and in FAA-approved training devices.

name: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
summary: An open-world action adventure whose physics and chemistry engines let fire, wind, electricity, temperature, and material properties combine, so puzzles and fights accept solutions the designers did not script.

name: Zoo Tycoon
summary: A zoo management game in which the player builds exhibits whose terrain, foliage, shelters, and toys must suit each species, balancing animal happiness against guest happiness and income.

name: Adaptive threat scaling
summary: Threat intensity is computed from a measure of the player's strength, such as wealth, population, time survived, or recent performance.

name: Adjacency scoring
summary: A placement's value is computed from a table of bonuses and penalties for the placements around it.

name: Advertising and awareness
summary: Spending on advertising raises a demand or awareness stock that decays without upkeep and scales how many customers arrive or buy.

name: Advisors
summary: In-world advisor characters monitor simulation indicators, summarize problems, and recommend actions.

name: Agent inspection
summary: Selecting an agent opens a panel that reveals its needs, mood contributors, current job, and the reasons behind its behavior.

name: Agent pathfinding
summary: Agents compute routes through space using movement costs, and the routes they choose shape congestion, travel time, and access.

name: Agent skills
summary: Agents gain skill through practice or training, and skill sets work speed, quality, and access to tasks.

name: Alerts feed
summary: A notification layer surfaces discrete events and threshold crossings with severity and a link to their location.

name: Animal husbandry
summary: Domestic animals are housed, fed, tended, and bred, and they yield products whose quantity and quality depend on their care.

name: Aspirations and wants
summary: An agent's long-term aspiration and current state generate short-horizon wants, and sometimes fears, whose fulfillment pays into a reward meter or currency.

name: Asynchronous shared regions
summary: Separate players' simulations affect each other asynchronously through shared regions, visits, or exchanges of goods and services.

name: Attribute-driven match engine
summary: Contest outcomes are simulated play by play from participant attributes, tactics, and randomness instead of being played directly.

name: Auctions
summary: Goods, land, or rights are allocated by bidding procedures in which players or agents compete on price under rules for timing, ties, and reserves.

name: Autonomy levels
summary: The degree to which agents act on their own is adjustable, from full free will to explicit commands only.

name: Blueprints
summary: Player-made layouts can be saved, stamped as build orders, copied, and shared as text or files.

name: Board confidence
summary: An evaluator such as a board, owner, or chairman sets expectations, updates a confidence stock from results against them, and fires the player below a threshold.

name: Treasury and budget
summary: A money stock with income and expense flows such as taxes, upkeep, wages, and service funding; a negative balance leads to debt or failure.

name: Byproducts and waste
summary: Production emits secondary outputs such as sludge, garbage, heat, or spent fuel that must be handled or they impair the system.

name: Care-dependent development
summary: A creature's or character's accumulated care or attribute history selects which form or outcome it develops into at each stage boundary, from a fixed branching table.

name: Career ladder
summary: Characters advance through ranked job levels by meeting skill, relationship, and performance requirements.

name: Causal breakdown tooltips
summary: Hovering a derived value shows the named modifiers that produce it, and terms inside the tooltip can be hovered in turn.

name: Citizen satisfaction
summary: An aggregate satisfaction score computed from services, conditions, and events modulates growth, productivity, and unrest.

name: Collection goals
summary: Catalogs of items, species, or bundles give the player sets to complete for rewards or recognition.

name: Combination discovery
summary: The player combines owned elements to discover the products of a hidden recipe graph, and finding recipes is itself the goal.

name: Comparative histograms
summary: A player's solution is plotted against distributions of other players' scores on several metrics.

name: Contagion
summary: Disease spreads between agents or regions via contact rates and moves hosts through compartments such as susceptible, infected, and recovered.

name: Content sharing
summary: Player creations such as buildings, creatures, or blueprints are uploaded, browsed, rated, and imported into other players' games.

name: Contracts and orders
summary: Discrete jobs with requirements, deadlines, and payouts, such as deliveries or commissions, drive income and planning.

name: Conveyor transport
summary: Items move continuously on belts or lanes with throughput limits, splitters, merges, and priorities.

name: Corruption leakage
summary: A corruption level driven by spending, administrative reach, or size removes a share of revenue or output until countermeasures bring it down.

name: Creature care
summary: The player directly feeds, cleans, and plays with a creature whose needs decay; neglect causes sickness, stunted growth, or death.

name: Creature learning
summary: A creature's behavior is learned from player reward and punishment or from neural adaptation over its life.

name: Crime and policing
summary: Crime levels arise from local conditions such as land value, density, or unemployment, and police coverage, prisons, and justice reduce them.

name: Crisis countdown
summary: A known future crisis such as a storm, winter, cure, or deadline is announced in advance, and the remaining time structures preparation.

name: Crop cultivation
summary: Planted crops progress through growth stages over days or seasons depending on water, soil, and season, then are harvested.

name: Crowd preferences
summary: Large visitor populations with individual preferences, budgets, and tolerances choose attractions and react with visible thoughts.

name: Culture and religion conversion
summary: Provinces or population groups carry culture and faith identities that drift or are converted by missionaries, policies, and rulers, changing unrest, opinion, and bonuses.

name: Customer value choice
summary: Customers choose among offerings by comparing price to perceived value and personal preference.

name: Daily action budget
summary: A per-day pool of energy, stamina, or time slots limits how many actions the player can take, and the day's end resets it and forces prioritization.

name: Daily schedules
summary: Agents follow time-blocked routines for work, sleep, and leisure that create rhythms of demand across the day.

name: Data overlays
summary: Map layers visualize hidden variables such as land value, pollution, coverage, or traffic.

name: Dated technology timeline
summary: New vehicle models, platforms, or products enter and leave availability on a calendar tied to in-game dates rather than to research, forcing fleet or platform renewal.

name: Day-night cycle
summary: A diurnal cycle changes light, visibility, temperature, and which agents are active, so activity follows the hour of the day.

name: Decoration and beauty
summary: Decorative objects and scenery carry beauty values that are aggregated over tiles, rooms, or radii and feed agent mood or ratings.

name: Delegation to AI managers
summary: Subsystems are handed to AI managers or governors that pursue player-set goals within bounds.

name: Delivery-time payment
summary: Payment for a delivery depends on cargo type, quantity, distance, and transit time, with each cargo losing value at its own rate the longer it travels.

name: Deposit depletion
summary: Extractable deposits hold finite quantities and run out, forcing expansion, relocation, or substitution.

name: Design performance rating
summary: Player-built designs are run or analyzed and scored on simulated metrics such as ride excitement, bridge stress, or cost and cycles.

name: Designation orders
summary: The player marks tiles or objects for work such as dig, chop, or build, and autonomous agents claim and execute the jobs.

name: Diagnose and repair
summary: The player inspects a machine, finds faulty parts with tools and tests, disassembles in order to reach them, and repairs or replaces them.

name: Diagnosis and treatment
summary: Patients present symptoms, examinations reduce uncertainty about a hidden condition, and the correct treatment cures it while wrong or late treatment harms.

name: Dilemma cards
summary: Discrete choice events present a situation with a few options that each shift meters, values, or flags in tradeoff.

name: Direct avatar control
summary: The player directly controls one embodied character's movement and actions in the simulated world.

name: Dynasty succession
summary: When the player character dies, play continues as an heir chosen by inheritance rules.

name: Education and workforce
summary: Education levels gate job types, and schooling converts the labor pool into higher levels over time.

name: Elections
summary: Periodic votes by simulated or real voters determine tenure or policy.

name: Embodied skill control
summary: Real-time motor skill operating a simulated mechanism, such as hand-flying, driving, or surgery, is the main challenge.

name: Equity and buyouts
summary: Companies issue shares whose price tracks performance, and players buy them for profit or accumulate a majority to take control of rivals.

name: Execution budget
summary: Player-written programs are metered against a simulated compute budget, such as CPU per tick, tick cost per operation, instruction slots, or RAM, which makes efficiency the scarce resource.

name: Faction diplomacy
summary: Factions hold relations with each other, and treaties, alliances, and wars follow from interests and opinion.

name: Falling-sand materials
summary: Every pixel or cell holds a material whose class rule makes it fall, flow, or rise by swapping with neighbors, with reactions layered on top.

name: Fire spread
summary: Fire ignites and spreads across flammable cells or objects at rates set by fuel, wind, and moisture, consuming what it burns.

name: Flight aerodynamics
summary: Lift, drag, thrust, and control-surface forces computed from airspeed and attitude govern aircraft motion.

name: Fluid and gas simulation
summary: Liquids and gases stored per cell or as fields flow, mix, and pressurize across space according to pressure and density differences.

name: Fluid pipe networks
summary: Fluids such as water, oil, sewage, or gas flow through pipes with pressure or throughput limits between producers and consumers.

name: Fog of war
summary: Parts of the world stay hidden or stale until observed by the player's units, structures, or sensors.

name: Food web
summary: Species eat and are eaten along a feeding graph, so populations rise, crash, and oscillate under predator-prey dynamics.

name: Forecasting
summary: The interface projects future states such as resource runway, budget balance, or upcoming weather.

name: Building placement
summary: The player places discrete structures on a grid or freely, and placement constraints turn layout into a spatial puzzle.

name: Generative content on demand
summary: A generative model creates new content such as text, items, recipes, or rules at runtime in response to player input.

name: God powers
summary: The player spends a power resource on miracles that alter terrain, weather, or creatures.

name: Goods consumption
summary: A population consumes goods at per-capita rates; unmet consumption lowers satisfaction or blocks advancement.

name: Gossip propagation
summary: Information about events spreads through social contacts, changing what agents know and believe.

name: Habitat suitability
summary: Species or crops thrive only where conditions such as terrain, temperature, water, and cover match their needs, scored per location.

name: Hand crafting
summary: The player or avatar combines carried components into items from a recipe list, gated by workstations and known recipes.

name: Hauling jobs
summary: Agents pick up and carry items between locations via a job queue, making hauling capacity a hidden throughput constraint.

name: Heat transfer
summary: Temperature diffuses between cells, materials, and objects by conductivity and heat capacity, and thresholds trigger phase changes and damage.

name: History chronicle
summary: The game records significant simulation events into a structured history that players can browse and other systems can reference.

name: Simulated history generation
summary: World generation simulates years to centuries of civilizations, figures, and events before play begins, producing the starting world.

name: Hydrology
summary: Water flows across terrain and through rivers by height differences, producing floods, droughts, irrigation, and dam management.

name: Immigration by attractiveness
summary: Population arrives or leaves based on attractiveness such as jobs, housing, and happiness relative to alternatives.

name: Injury body model
summary: Bodies are hierarchies of parts with their own damage, and wounds, bleeding, infection, and prosthetics change capacities such as moving and manipulation.

name: Interest groups
summary: Factions within a polity have clout and preferences over policies, and their approval gates what the player can do.

name: Labor market
summary: Workers fill jobs by type and education; mismatches create unemployment or labor shortages that throttle production.

name: Land value
summary: Each location's value is computed from nearby amenities, nuisances, and access, and it drives density and building upgrades.

name: Lifecycle and aging
summary: Agents are born, age through life stages with different capabilities, and die.

name: Loans and debt
summary: Capital can be borrowed at interest with repayment schedules, so leverage accelerates both growth and failure.

name: Loss on death
summary: When a character or ship is destroyed, its carried or fitted assets are lost or dropped at the death site for the owner or others to recover, with insurance or retrieval rules as softeners.

name: Machine boosting
summary: Per-machine modifiers such as modules, beacons, clock speed, or coatings trade extra power, scarce items, or currency for faster or more productive machines.

name: Material interactions
summary: A rule table defines how elements such as fire, water, and electricity change materials and each other on contact.

name: Megaproject sink
summary: A terminal construction absorbs very large quantities of produced goods in staged phases and serves as the long-run goal and output sink of a production game.

name: Memories and thoughts
summary: Events create itemized, time-limited mood modifiers or lasting memories that shape later behavior.

name: Milestone unlocks
summary: Reaching thresholds such as population, output, or score unlocks new buildings, areas, or features.

name: Military operations
summary: Units with modeled sensors, weapons, platforms, and doctrine conduct operations at operational fidelity, mostly under player orders and automated behavior.

name: Modding API
summary: Official hooks for scripts and data definitions let players change and extend the simulation's content and rules.

name: Modular assembly
summary: The player builds machines, vehicles, or creatures from parts whose stats and physical arrangement determine how the result behaves.

name: Mood and breakdowns
summary: Mood aggregates needs, memories, and environment, and crossing thresholds triggers mental breaks or inspired performance.

name: Natural-language interaction
summary: The player communicates with characters by free text or voice, and the system interprets intent and responds.

name: Natural selection
summary: Differential survival and reproduction by fitness shifts trait distributions across generations.

name: Needs decay
summary: Each agent has needs such as hunger, energy, social, and fun that decay over time and are restored by actions.

name: Negotiation
summary: The player and an AI party exchange offers and counteroffers over wages, prices, or contract terms against the AI's hidden reservation value until a deal is struck or talks fail.

name: Off-screen life progression
summary: Households or agents outside the player's active simulation advance through life events on a cheap stochastic model, so the world changes between visits.

name: Opinion modifiers
summary: Opinions are sums of named, decaying modifiers from events and traits, itemized for the player.

name: Orbital mechanics
summary: Bodies move under gravity, and maneuvers spend delta-v to change orbits, intercepts, and transfers.

name: Periodic ticks
summary: Some state changes, such as budgets, harvests, or growth, resolve in batches at fixed intervals like a month or a year rather than continuously.

name: Permadeath
summary: Death of agents or the avatar is permanent, and the save system prevents undoing it.

name: Persistent shared world
summary: A server-side world keeps running and keeps its state for many players, whether or not any one player is logged in.

name: Personality traits
summary: Fixed or slow-changing traits change each agent's needs, preferences, and available actions.

name: Planetary climate
summary: Planet-scale variables such as atmospheric composition, temperature, sea level, and biosphere evolve under coupled feedbacks and can be deliberately altered.

name: Player-driven markets
summary: Players post buy and sell orders in shared order books, and prices emerge from player behavior.

name: Player legislation
summary: Players author, propose, and vote on rules that the game then enforces inside a shared world, such as taxes, bans, and permits.

name: Player organizations
summary: Players form corporations, guilds, or governments with membership, roles, permissions, and shared assets.

name: Player programming
summary: The player writes code in a language the game executes to control units, machines, or the world.

name: Policy influence network
summary: Policies, indicators, and voter groups connect through a weighted causal graph with delays.

name: Policy toggles
summary: Enactable laws or policies change simulation rules with explicit tradeoffs.

name: Political capital
summary: An abstract governing currency accrues each period from leaders, factions, or population welfare and is spent on policy changes, edicts, and other state actions.

name: Pollution spread
summary: Pollution emitted by sources accumulates and diffuses across land, water, or air cells and harms health, land value, or growth, or provokes threats.

name: Population strata
summary: The population is divided into classes or tiers with distinct needs, roles, and upgrade paths.

name: Power allocation
summary: The player splits a fixed power budget among a vehicle's subsystems in real time, trading shields, weapons, engines, and life support against each other.

name: Power grid
summary: Generators produce energy that is distributed over a connected network to consumers; shortfalls cause brownouts or shutdowns.

name: Procedural build assist
summary: Coarse player input such as a block or a drawn wall is turned into detailed, organic structures by procedural rules.

name: Procedural characters
summary: Characters are generated with names, backstories, traits, skills, and appearance sampled from constrained tables or grammars.

name: Procedural checklists
summary: Operating simulated equipment requires performing ordered steps on modeled controls that mirror real procedures, with system states gating each step.

name: Procedural terrain
summary: Maps are generated from a seed through noise, erosion, climate, and placement rules.

name: Product development
summary: The player configures a product's features, and a simulated market scores it against trends, quality, and competition.

name: Production chains
summary: Buildings or machines convert input goods into output goods via fixed recipes and cycle times, forming multi-step dependency trees.

name: Programming by demonstration
summary: An agent or vehicle learns a routine by recording the player performing it, and the recording becomes a replayable, sometimes editable, program.

name: Projectile ballistics
summary: Shots are simulated as projectiles in flight with velocity, gravity, drag, and penetration, so range, angle, and lead decide hits rather than an instant trace or a dice roll.

name: Public transit lines
summary: Player-drawn lines with stops and vehicles carry passengers whose ridership depends on coverage, frequency, and transfers.

name: PvP security zones
summary: A shared world is divided into zones whose rules set whether players may attack each other and what an aggressor pays, such as NPC police response or lost standing.

name: Quality tiers
summary: Produced items carry quality grades derived from inputs, worker skill, or chance, scaling their value or effect.

name: Raid defense
summary: Settlements defend against periodic attacks with walls, turrets, traps, and fighters placed and commanded by the player.

name: Rail signaling
summary: Block and path signals partition track so trains can share it without collision; throughput depends on signal design.

name: Random disasters
summary: Stochastic disasters such as fires, floods, earthquakes, storms, or meteors strike at random times and places and damage the system.

name: RCI demand
summary: A demand signal for residential, commercial, and industrial land derived from the balance of jobs, workers, and goods.

name: Real-time clock
summary: Game time follows the real-world clock and calendar, so the world advances, ages, and holds events while the game is closed.

name: Real-world data feeds
summary: Simulation state is initialized or driven at runtime by external real-world data such as map imagery, elevation, star catalogs, live weather, or live traffic instead of authored or procedural content.

name: Relationship values
summary: Pairwise numeric affinity between characters changes with interactions and drives social choices.

name: Renewable regrowth
summary: Harvested stocks such as forests, fish, game, and soil regenerate over time at density-dependent rates, allowing sustainable yield or overexploitation.

name: Reputation
summary: A standing value with a faction or the public changes access, prices, and how others respond.

name: Request-provider logistics
summary: Containers declare per-item requests and supplies, and a dispatcher sends drones or robots from providers to requesters without fixed routes.

name: Resource extraction
summary: Workers or machines harvest raw materials from map nodes (ore, trees, fish, oil) at rates set by tools, labor, and node richness.

name: Rigid-body physics
summary: Objects with mass and inertia move under forces and collide, constrained by contacts and joints solved each step.

name: Rival firms
summary: AI or player competitors contest markets, prices, and assets; market share decides who wins.

name: Road networks
summary: Roads and paths define connectivity; buildings must connect to function, and travel cost depends on network geometry.

name: Romance and family
summary: Agents court, partner, marry, and form families according to compatibility and relationship state.

name: Room recognition
summary: Enclosed spaces are detected by flood fill and classified into room types by their size and contents, and the type grants effects.

name: Rule-checking inspection
summary: The player checks documents, people, or cargo against a rulebook that changes over time, under time pressure, with penalties for errors.

name: Scenario objectives
summary: Preset maps or situations come with explicit goals, constraints, and often a deadline.

name: Scouting knowledge
summary: Entity attributes are known only with uncertainty that scouting effort reduces.

name: Seasonal world reset
summary: A shared world runs for a bounded season and is then wiped and restarted, often with rule changes carried into the next season.

name: Seasons
summary: A seasonal calendar cycles conditions such as temperature, daylight, and growing windows that govern growth, demand, and risk.

name: Service coverage
summary: Service buildings such as police, fire, clinics, and schools satisfy demand within a radius or network distance, up to a capacity.

name: Service queues
summary: Agents wait in lines for limited-capacity services; waiting time feeds back into satisfaction and throughput.

name: Signal circuits
summary: In-world wires, sensors, and logic elements carry signals that read machine state and control machines.

name: Smart objects
summary: Objects advertise the need satisfaction they offer, and agents query nearby objects to decide what to do.

name: Social exchanges
summary: Discrete social moves such as flirt, insult, or apologize have preconditions on social state and norms, and they update relationships.

name: Soft-body deformation
summary: Objects built from mass nodes and spring beams bend, crumple, and break under stress, and deformation persists.

name: Spoilage
summary: Perishable goods lose value or rot over time depending on storage conditions such as temperature and containers.

name: Stability and unrest
summary: Grievances accumulate into unrest that triggers protests, strikes, or revolt.

name: Staff hiring and rosters
summary: The player hires individual staff with skills, traits, and wages to operate a facility or team.

name: Statistical combat resolution
summary: Battles between units resolve from attack, defense, morale, terrain, and random rolls in rounds rather than from physics or modeled sensors and weapons.

name: Stats dashboards
summary: Graphs and tables show the recorded history of simulation variables over selectable time windows.

name: Stimulus attraction
summary: Player actions emit sound or light stimuli with a radius and decay, and agents that perceive them move toward the source, so managing emissions is part of survival.

name: Storage and buffers
summary: Goods occupy finite storage; buffers decouple producers from consumers, and full storage blocks production.

name: Storyteller director
summary: A director AI chooses which events to fire and when, pacing them by a model of tension and the current state.

name: Stress accumulation
summary: A slow per-agent stress stock integrates negative experiences scaled by personality and, as it crosses levels, triggers breaks or lasting changes.

name: Structural integrity
summary: Structures carry support values or loads propagated from the ground, and elements that lose support or exceed their limits collapse.

name: Subsystem damage
summary: A vehicle or ship is a set of named components with their own integrity, and damage to one removes its capacity, such as power, thrust, shields, or sensors, until it is repaired.

name: Supply-demand pricing
summary: Prices adjust to supply and demand, so scarcity raises prices and gluts lower them.

name: Supply lines
summary: Remote units or outposts need a continuous connection to a supply source; cutting the connection causes attrition.

name: Surface work tools
summary: The player applies a tool to surfaces to clean, paint, or strip them, and a per-surface coverage state shows visible progress toward completion.

name: Survival meters
summary: The avatar's bodily stocks such as hunger, thirst, warmth, and fatigue deplete over time and, if unmanaged, drain health and kill.

name: Taxation
summary: Player-set tax rates convert economic activity into revenue at the cost of growth, happiness, or competitiveness.

name: Tech tree
summary: A research or unlock graph gates buildings, recipes, or abilities behind prerequisites and accumulated research.

name: Terraforming
summary: The player raises, lowers, flattens, or repaints terrain, usually at a cost, to make land usable or to reshape water and paths.

name: Terrain deformation
summary: Wheels, feet, and impacts displace soft ground such as mud and snow, and the persistent ruts change traction for later passes.

name: Territorial control
summary: Map regions have an owner and a current controller; occupation flips control in war, and peace, purchase, or integration transfers ownership at a cost in time, unrest, or political currency.

name: Track laying
summary: The player builds rail or coaster track segment by segment under grade, curvature, terrain, and cost constraints, and vehicles then run on the resulting path.

name: Trade routes
summary: Goods are exchanged between settlements, regions, or foreign markets along routes with price differences, tariffs, and transit time.

name: Traffic congestion
summary: Trips route over a capacitated network; volume beyond capacity raises travel time and delays services and deliveries.

name: Trait inheritance
summary: Offspring inherit traits or genes from their parents with recombination, variation, or mutation.

name: Travel mode choice
summary: Agents choose among walking, cycling, driving, and transit for each trip by comparing time, money, and comfort costs, which sets how demand splits across networks.

name: Triggered event chains
summary: Authored event templates fire when state conditions hold, and their outcomes schedule follow-up events that chain into multi-step stories.

name: Turn structure
summary: The simulation advances in discrete turns, each divided into ordered phases in which players decide and the world then resolves.

name: Unit commands
summary: The player issues direct orders to specific units or agents, overriding their autonomous behavior.

name: Utility action selection
summary: Agents choose actions by scoring options against needs and context, then picking the highest or sampling among high scores.

name: Pause and speed control
summary: The player pauses the simulation and switches between speed multipliers, trading attention against elapsed game time.

name: Vehicle dynamics
summary: Tire, suspension, drivetrain, and weight-transfer models compute vehicle handling from forces at each wheel.

name: Vehicle routes and schedules
summary: Vehicles are assigned ordered stops with load and unload rules to move goods or passengers between nodes.

name: Vertical layers
summary: The world has stacked layers such as z-levels, floors, or underground networks, and rules connect what happens between them.

name: Villager requests
summary: Characters generate small requests or quests from templates whose parameters are filled from simulation state, with rewards and deadlines.

name: Voxel destruction
summary: The world is built from small destructible units that can be removed, broken loose, and burned anywhere.

name: Walker service delivery
summary: Services are delivered by agents walking routes from their building, so coverage depends on where walkers actually go.

name: War score and peace terms
summary: Each war tracks a score or exhaustion level from battles, occupation, and war goals, and that value caps what a peace settlement can demand or forces capitulation.

name: Wear and breakdown
summary: Assets lose condition with use and age, breakdown risk rises as condition falls, and maintenance or repair restores it.

name: Weather
summary: Weather states such as rain, storms, snow, wind, and temperature change over time and modify activities and other systems.

name: Work priorities
summary: The player sets which agents do which job types in what order, and agents self-assign from that priority table.

name: Zoning
summary: The player paints land-use zones, and the simulation decides whether and what to build, upgrade, or abandon on each zoned lot.

name: LLM-guided evolutionary program search
summary: An LLM proposes edits to code, an automated evaluator scores each candidate, and an evolutionary database keeps the best and most diverse programs, finding heuristics and constructions that beat human-designed ones.

name: Agent-based automated playtesting and balancing
summary: Studios train imitation, reinforcement learning, and search agents to play builds, estimating level difficulty, pass and churn rates, progression pacing, map coverage, and exploits before players reach them.

name: Automated generation of game rules and mechanics
summary: Systems that write complete game rule sets as code in a description language, using evolution or language models to propose rules and self-play agents to score balance, decisiveness, and strategic depth before a human sees them.

name: Language models grounded in strategic planning for negotiation games
summary: Meta's Cicero couples a dialogue language model with a planning engine that infers other players' intentions from the board and conversation, so its free-text negotiation proposes and follows concrete joint plans, reaching human-level Diplomacy.

name: Grammar-constrained decoding for valid game actions
summary: Decoding that masks every token which cannot extend a valid string of a schema, regular expression, or grammar, so a model's output always parses as a legal game action or data record.

name: Continuous cellular automata and foundation-model search for artificial life
summary: Continuous cellular automata such as Lenia and mass-conserving Flow-Lenia produce lifelike self-organizing creatures, and ASAL uses vision-language foundation models to search their rule spaces for phenomena described in text or for open-ended novelty.

name: Deep reinforcement learning policies for NPC opponents and navigation
summary: Neural control policies trained with deep reinforcement learning inside the game's own simulation drive opponents and NPCs, as with Sony AI's Gran Turismo Sophy, a selectable rival in Gran Turismo 7 since 2023.

name: Differentiable simulation
summary: Simulators written so automatic differentiation returns gradients of an outcome with respect to initial state, controls, or rule parameters, replacing black-box search with gradient descent for tuning and inverse design.

name: Diffusion and autoregressive neural game engines
summary: Action-conditioned generative models trained on recordings of one existing game predict each next frame from recent frames and player input, so the model itself plays the role of the game engine.

name: 3D Gaussian Splatting
summary: Scenes are represented as millions of anisotropic 3D Gaussians optimized from photos and rasterized in real time, giving photoreal captured or generated environments at 1080p and 30+ fps.

name: Generalist instructable game agents (SIMA)
summary: Agents that read screen pixels and natural-language instructions and output keyboard and mouse actions across many commercial 3D games, with later versions reasoning, conversing, and improving through self-generated tasks.

name: Prompt-to-persistent 3D world generation
summary: Models such as World Labs Marble and HunyuanWorld turn text, images, video, or coarse 3D blockouts into persistent explorable scenes exported as Gaussian splats and meshes with collision proxies.

name: Generative agents (memory stream, reflection, planning)
summary: LLM-driven characters that store observations in a natural-language memory stream, retrieve them by recency, importance, and relevance, synthesize reflections, and plan their day top-down.

name: Genie foundation world models
summary: Google DeepMind's Genie models generate playable worlds from a text or image prompt and render them in real time from player input, with Genie 3 reaching 720p at 24 fps and about a minute of visual memory.

name: Graph network simulators and neural operators
summary: Learned simulators that predict the next state of particles, meshes, or continuous fields with message-passing networks or Fourier-space operators, trained on numerical solver output and run 10-1000x faster than that solver.

name: LLM models of individual human choice
summary: Language models conditioned on interviews or fine-tuned on millions of experimental choices that predict how specific people or populations answer surveys, play economic games, and choose in decision tasks.

name: Regret minimization and search for imperfect-information games
summary: Self-play algorithms that minimize counterfactual regret over information sets, refined by real-time subgame search, compute hard-to-exploit strategies that bluff and hide information and beat top humans at poker, Stratego, and Scotland Yard.

name: Learned level and map generation (PCGRL, MarioGPT, LLM generators)
summary: Generators trained by reinforcement learning or on example levels, including small and large language models that emit tile maps from text prompts, produce playable levels and maps without hand-written generation rules.

name: Learned kinematic motion synthesis
summary: Neural networks generate or compress kinematic character animation, as in Ubisoft's learned motion matching, EA's HyperMotion, and inZOI's motion extraction from uploaded video.

name: Many-agent LLM societies
summary: Simulations of hundreds to a million LLM-driven agents with concurrent cognitive modules, shared environments, and message buses that produce role specialization, rule changes, cultural spread, and polarization.

name: LLM explanation of simulation state
summary: Language models that read simulation state, modifier breakdowns, agent traces, or event logs and answer why and what-if questions or summarize what happened for players and designers.

name: LLM game master and narrative director
summary: A language model that adjudicates player and NPC intentions, decides outcomes, generates events and quests, and narrates them, either free-form or checked against a typed world state and canon.

name: LLM-adjudicated state transitions (LLM as game mechanic)
summary: A language model computes the outcome of an interaction (two elements combined, an action on an object) from a text description of the inputs, with results cached so every player sees the same rule.

name: Massively parallel GPU simulation
summary: Simulators that keep thousands of world instances as tensors on a GPU or TPU and step them all in one kernel, raising throughput to millions of steps per second for agent training and Monte Carlo sweeps.

name: Mean field games and mean-field learning
summary: Mean field game theory replaces an N-player game with one representative agent responding to the population distribution, and recent learning methods compute these equilibria for state spaces of hundreds of billions of states.

name: Machine-learned weather forecasting
summary: Neural networks trained on decades of atmospheric reanalysis forecast global weather 10-15 days ahead in seconds to minutes on one accelerator, matching or beating physics-based operational models on most verification targets.

name: Self-play planning with learned models (AlphaZero, MuZero, Dreamer)
